headline: Recommended four appointments, including Lydia Warren as Arts & Culture director; kept two items in committee.
summary: Candidates for the Board of Assessors, the Condominium Review Board, and Director of Arts & Culture answered councilors' questions. Ashley Tienken's appointment to the Affordable Housing Trust and a City Clerk hiring order were kept in committee.

Recommended approval of Christopher Gaeta's appointment to the Board of Assessors, 4-0.

## City of Somerville, Massachusetts City Council Confirmation of Appointments and Personnel Matters Committee Meeting Minutes

Monday, November 16, 2026

6:00 PM

This meeting was held virtually via Zoom and was called to order at 6:00 pm by Chair Mbah and adjourned at 7:27 pm with a roll call vote of 4 in favor (Councilors Hardt, Link, Ewen-Campen and Mbah), none opposed, and 1 absent (Councilor McLaughlin).

Also present: Lauren Chapman - Condominium Review Board Staff Liaison, Francis Golden - Board of Assessors Chairman, Anne Gill - Director of People Operations and Delaney Fisher-Cassiol - Clerk of Committees

Roll Call

- Present: Ward Seven City Councilor Emily Hardt, City Councilor At
- Large Jon Link, Ward Three City Councilor Ben
- Ewen-Campen and City Councilor At Large Wilfred N.

Mbah

Absent:

Ward One City Councilor Matthew McLaughlin

1. Committee

Approval of the Minutes of the Confirmation of Appointments and Minutes

Personnel Matters Committee Meeting of July 6, 2026.

(ID # 26-1213 )

- RESULT: ACCEPTED
- AYE:

- Ward Seven City Councilor Hardt, City Councilor At Large
- Link, Ward Three City Councilor Ewen-Campen and City
- Councilor At Large Mbah
- ABSENT: Ward One City Councilor McLaughlin

2. Order

By Councilor Mbah

(ID # 25-1423 ) That the City Clerk implement the hiring practices detailed within for

positions in the City Council and City Clerk Departments.

RESULT: KEPT IN COMMITTEE

3. Mayor's Request Requesting confirmation of the appointment of Ashley Tienken to the (ID # 26-1405 ) Affordable Housing Trust.

RESULT: KEPT IN COMMITTEE

4. Mayor's Request Requesting confirmation of the appointment of Christopher Gaeta to the (ID # 26-1455 ) Board of Assessors.

Francis Golden, Chair of the Board of Assessors and Chief Assessor for the City, noted that Christopher Gaeta understands all facets of the role and that the board's busiest period is January through May, when additional support

is needed to review filings and assist with other responsibilities. Mr. Gaeta has nearly 12 years of experience in assessing, including eight years as

Director of Assessing for the City of Lynn. He previously worked for a local affordable housing developer.

- In response to a question from Chair Mbah, Mr. Gaeta explained that he

works to guide people through the process and ensure transparency by providing them with all relevant information. He noted that applicants

whose incomes fall below certain thresholds may qualify for an exemption and that he wants to help residents in any way possible. He acknowledged

that the work can be challenging because assessment decisions directly affect people's financial circumstances, but finding ways to help residents makes the work rewarding. Chair Golden clarified that the Board of Assessors consists of three members, with the chair overseeing the other two assessors. He also noted that the position is part-time and pays $10,000

annually. In response to questions from Councilor Hardt, Mr. Gaeta explained that he is interested in learning about and applying his skills in a new community. Having seen affordability challenges across different

communities, he welcomes the opportunity to take on a new challenge and continue growing professionally.

RESULT: RECOMMENDED TO BE APPROVED AYE:

- Ward Seven City Councilor Hardt, City Councilor At Large
- Link, Ward Three City Councilor Ewen-Campen and City
- Councilor At Large Mbah
- ABSENT: Ward One City Councilor McLaughlin

5. Mayor's Request Requesting confirmation of the appointment of Gary Rogers to the (ID # 26-1533 ) Condominium Review Board.

- Lauren Chapman, Staff Liaison to the Condo Review Board, introduced

Gary Rogers, noting that he has experience navigating the housing system and is involved with the Somerville Community Action Agency. She

highlighted his strong understanding of tenants' rights and housing issues, as well as his ability to approach matters impartially.

Mr. Rogers shared that he has lived in Somerville as a renter for nearly three decades and has personally experienced the eviction process. He expressed

appreciation for the support he has received from the community, noting that the City has stood by him in his efforts to remain in his apartment. He

described his involvement in tenant advocacy and acknowledged that the position requires an open mind and a thorough understanding of the ordinance. He has taken the time to learn about tenant law and is also

interested in understanding the laws governing landlords. He noted that he is retiring in a year or so and wants to continue playing a role in housing

advocacy and supporting the community. Chair Mbah asked how he would ensure tenants are protected throughout the process. Mr. Rogers explained

that his own experience with eviction motivated him to become more knowledgeable about housing laws. He committed to familiarizing himself

with the ordinance and its requirements. Having experienced bias himself, he wants to help ensure that others are not subject to similar treatment, as he understands firsthand how that feels. Councilors Link and Ewen-Campen

- expressed support for his appointment.

RESULT: RECOMMENDED TO BE APPROVED AYE:

- Ward Seven City Councilor Hardt, City Councilor At Large
- Link, Ward Three City Councilor Ewen-Campen and City
- Councilor At Large Mbah
- ABSENT: Ward One City Councilor McLaughlin

6. Mayor's Request Requesting confirmation of the appointment of Fatima Climaco to the (ID # 26-1534 ) Condominium Review Board.

- Lauren Chapman, Staff Liaison to the Condo Review Board, noted that there

are currently two vacancies for Somerville residents who are renters. She introduced Fatima Climaco, noting that she is a lifelong Somerville resident who is raising her children in the city. She is also bilingual in English and Spanish and can connect with residents from different backgrounds.

Ms. Climaco expressed appreciation for the consideration and reiterated that she has lived in Somerville her entire life and has strong connections

throughout the community. Chair Mbah thanked her for stepping forward to serve, noting that public service is a shared commitment and that diversity of backgrounds strengthens the city. Chair Mbah asked how she would ensure

fairness and equity, particularly for vulnerable residents. Ms. Climaco stated that she believes everyone should be treated equally and that vulnerable

residents are just as important as the rest of the community, though they may need additional attention. She described herself as caring and compassionate, with a strong desire to help others and ensure everyone feels welcome and at home in Somerville. Councilor Ewen-Campen thanked Ms.

Climaco for volunteering and asked what drew her to the position. Ms.

- Climaco explained that she subscribes to the city's affordable housing

notifications because she likes to stay informed and involved. When she received an email about the board vacancies, she saw it as an opportunity to become more involved and help the community. In response to a question

from Councilor Link, Ms. Climaco shared that she has lived in affordable housing and understands its importance, noting that without it, she would

not have been able to afford a home for herself and her children. She also described the evolution of affordable housing in Somerville, observing that much of the housing available today consists of condominiums. She viewed

the board position as an opportunity to contribute her experience and become more involved in an area with which she is very familiar.

RESULT: RECOMMENDED TO BE APPROVED AYE:

- Ward Seven City Councilor Hardt, City Councilor At Large
- Link, Ward Three City Councilor Ewen-Campen and City
- Councilor At Large Mbah
- ABSENT: Ward One City Councilor McLaughlin

7. Mayor's Request Requesting confirmation of the appointment of Lydia Warren as Director of (ID # 26-1605 ) Arts & Culture.

Anne Gill, Director of People Operations, introduced Dr. Lydia Warren, noting that she has experience directing a museum, has released numerous

publications, received grants, and has served as a board member. Dr. Warren shared that she grew up in Franklin, Massachusetts, and that Davis Square

was one of the first places where she played music and made her first recordings. As a Massachusetts-based professional musician, she wanted to remain involved in the arts. Her dissertation research focused on equity in the arts, particularly economic equity. In response to a question from Chair Mbah, Dr. Warren discussed the Cultural Council grant program, noting that

Somerville's program is more robust due to funding from Encore. She believes the City could improve outreach to ensure more residents are aware of and able to access these opportunities. She emphasized the importance of ensuring the community benefits from cultural events and expressed interest in mapping Somerville's local arts landscape and supporting the work

- already underway. She also noted that internships for Bunker Hill

Community College students have been inconsistent and would like to make them more regular so students can better understand and engage with the city's arts ecosystem.

Chair Mbah asked about her priorities and how she would evaluate the impact of arts and culture in Somerville. Dr. Warren identified advocacy for the Cultural Trust as one priority. She also noted that the Arts and Culture division plans to undertake strategic planning with a consultant for the first time since 2008. She explained that this process would also provide an

opportunity for team building and help colleagues better understand each other's work. She also identified the Armory as another priority, emphasizing the importance of ensuring it remains functional, sustainable, economically viable, and accessible to both the arts community and the general public. Councilor Ewen-Campen noted that the position is highly

public-facing and asked how Dr. Warren would build trust and relationships with residents. Dr. Warren discussed her background in ethnomusicology

and her interest in understanding how music communities develop and the social connections surrounding them. She enjoys meeting people, listening

to their experiences, and learning about their historical and cultural backgrounds. She emphasized that each person's perspective is their own

truth and that her role is to understand those perspectives and consider how to amplify residents' needs. She noted that sometimes the first step is simply listening deeply and validating people's experiences. Having experienced

situations where things did not go her way, she also understands the importance of empathy. Councilor Ewen-Campen expressed appreciation for

her commitment and noted that the Council is available to support her in any way possible. Councilor Link asked where she sees opportunities for the City. Dr. Warren pointed to the City's role in organizing and supporting

events and discussed ways to make those opportunities more accessible to residents. She noted that while the City often organizes large-scale events, residents who want to organize their own events may need additional

support. She emphasized the importance of making events more scalable and replicable, noting that residents may be less likely to organize festivals or other events if they do not have the knowledge or resources to do so.

RESULT: RECOMMENDED TO BE APPROVED AYE:

- Ward Seven City Councilor Hardt, City Councilor At Large
- Link, Ward Three City Councilor Ewen-Campen and City
- Councilor At Large Mbah
- ABSENT: Ward One City Councilor McLaughlin
